text:
Neuroscience has long inspired artificial intelligence. Now, we're using AI to better understand our brains.

In our latest podcast episode, researchers @eckstein_maria and @neuro_kim explore how machine learning can help uncover how we make decisions.

Timecodes:
00:00 Introduction
01:11 Using AI to understand the brain
10:14 Exploring reward learning
27:50 Automating model discovery
34:50 Comparing species and future directions
42:11 Hannah’s thoughts

Gemini 4 Neon coded a Rube Goldberg machine inside a 1980s arcade.

Built in @Antigravity with simulated physics and a Lyria 3.5 synth track, it runs through pinball bumpers before lighting up glass tubes.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen built an interactive 3D globe that turns live lightning strikes into ambient music.

Try it here →

Gemini 4 Neon recreated Alan Turing’s 1936 study at @Cambridge_Uni in interactive 3D.

Using archival photos in @Antigravity, the model built Room X.8 at King’s College with a running Universal Turing Machine.

Gemini 4 Neon coded a ski simulator based on real Mont Blanc terrain.

Built in @Antigravity with custom shaders and zero pre-made 3D models, it renders carved snow and avalanches live.

Try it now →

Gemini 4 Hydrogen turned Google Sheets into a pixel-art canvas.

Using @Antigravity, the model shrank thousands of cells to create animated scenes.
